extraction.name: RoboFAC Dataset
extraction.description: A large-scale and diverse dataset for question-answering on robot failure videos, comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments. The dataset covers six types of failures across three hierarchical levels (task planning error, motion planning error, and execution control error), and includes eight question types targeting task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao (School of AI, Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Xiamen University; Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen)
extraction.citeAs: Lu, W., Ye, M., Ye, Z., Tao, R., Yang, S., & Zhao, B. (2025). RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction. arXiv:2505.12224v3 [cs.RO].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Simulation data was collected for 14 robotic tasks in the ManiSkill environment, augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Expert policies were defined by specifying target end-effector poses for each substage, and failure data was generated by replacing the expert policy with code snippets that produce erroneous trajectories. Real-world data was collected for 6 tasks via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm. Each video was accompanied by a corresponding textual description including the substage where failure occurred, the taxonomy of failure, and a detailed textual explanation of the error.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed, resulting in trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions. Manual data cleaning was performed and approximately 75% of the collected simulation data was retained.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Simulation data from the ManiSkill environment augmented with YCB Object Dataset objects and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Real-world data collected via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm. The dataset includes 8,960 failure trajectories in the simulated environment, 480 failure trajectories in the real world, 1,160 successful trajectories from simulation, and 122 successful trajectories from real-world executions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Failure data was generated by replacing the original expert policy with a code snippet that generates an erroneous trajectory at a selected substage, causing the overall robotic task to fail. Variations in backgrounds and camera viewpoints were introduced to increase visual diversity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manual data cleaning was performed on simulation data to remove trajectories that did not align with their corresponding textual descriptions, retaining approximately 75% of the collected data. For the training and testing split, 60K QA pairs were randomly sampled from the simulated RoboFAC dataset as the training set, with the remaining QA pairs used for evaluation (10K simulated QA pairs and 8K real-world QA pairs).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Raw data was annotated to construct video-based QA samples for eight question types. For five question types (task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, and failure locating), reference answers were directly extracted from the textual descriptions associated with the videos. For the remaining three types (failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction), GPT-4o was used with both the video and its corresponding textual description as inputs to generate reference answers. All GPT-4o outputs were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality. Five question templates were provided for each question type, with one randomly sampled per QA pair.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: GPT-4o (for generating failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction annotations); manual human review and correction
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All outputs from GPT-4o were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality. For evaluation, GPT-4 was used as a scoring agent assessing model responses across three dimensions (correctness, relevance, completeness) on a 1-5 scale, configured with temperature 0.2 and Top-P 1.0.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each video sample is annotated with up to eight QA pairs corresponding to eight question types: task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, failure locating, failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o (used for generating failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction annotations); GPT-4 (used as LLM scoring agent for evaluation)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Model and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/MINT-SJTU/RoboFAC. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The RoboFAC framework aims to improve robotic failure recovery in open-world scenarios, enabling VLA models to better handle failures and recover from errors. This could improve the reliability and safety of robotic systems deployed in real-world environments.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is predominantly based on simulation environments (14 simulated tasks vs. 6 real-world tasks), which may introduce a sim-to-real gap. The model is never trained on real-world data, and the real-world test set includes two tasks never encountered during training (InsertCylinder and PlaceCube).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current robot failure datasets are limited in scope; the integration of the RoboFAC model into the VLA-controlled robotic system is not yet seamless. The success rate in real-world tasks remains subject to further enhancement, largely due to the VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions. The model is applied exclusively to VLA models and not to hierarchical policies.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training (60K QA pairs from simulated data), Testing and Evaluation (10K simulated QA pairs and 8K real-world QA pairs on the RoboFAC benchmark), Fine-tuning multimodal large language models for robotic failure analysis and correction, and integration as an external critic in real-world VLA robotic control pipelines.
